Trap: Comparing list prices without workload profiles. Model the same three or four representative workloads on both before deciding.

• Which system is the governance source of truth for PHI, and how are permissions mirrored or re-implemented on the other side?
  • Which workloads need Spark streaming, ML or agents (Databricks strengths) versus Power BI-centric self-service (Fabric strengths)?
  • Does the team have the skills to operate both, and what is the exit cost if one is dropped?

cards.q: Which Fabric feature exposes Unity Catalog tables in Fabric without copying data, and what is its status?
cards.a: Mirrored Azure Databricks catalog, which is generally available.

cards.q: Will a Unity Catalog table with column masks appear in a Fabric mirrored catalog?
cards.a: No; tables with row-level security or column masking policies are unsupported for mirroring.

cards.q: How does Databricks read Fabric Lakehouse tables in place?
cards.a: OneLake catalog federation: a onelake connection plus a foreign catalog, read-only.

cards.q: What is the core pricing difference between Databricks and Fabric?
cards.a: Databricks charges per-workload DBU consumption; Fabric charges for a shared capacity SKU that all workloads draw from.

concepts.n: Unity Gateway, Model Serving and AI functions in SQL
concepts.s: Unity Gateway is the control plane for governed access to models, MCP tools and skills with routing, spend limits and audit, Model Serving hosts custom models as endpoints, and AI functions bring model inference into SQL for batch enrichment of governed tables.

x.b:
• Unity Gateway (API and developer tools GA September 2026): one place to govern Databricks-hosted foundation models (for example system-provided pay-per-token services in system.ai), your own provider accounts (OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Azure Foundry), MCP servers and skills. It provides routing, usage and spend tracking, budgets and spend limits, PII masking, guardrails and audit logs. It also governs coding agents through the ug CLI.
  • Foundation model capacity: pay-per-token or on-demand provisioned throughput.
  • Custom model serving: MLflow models from Unity Catalog served on CPU or GPU endpoints with traffic splitting, inference tables and optional scale to zero (not recommended for production because capacity is not guaranteed).
  • AI functions: ai_query (GA June 2026) for any supported model, plus task functions such as ai_parse_document, ai_extract and ai_classify (GA June 2026), ai_mask, ai_summarize, ai_forecast, and Beta functions like ai_search and ai_enrich. AI functions Unity Catalog permissions went GA October 2026.

x.t: Example: batch extraction from clinical notes
x.b:
SELECT note_id,
       ai_classify(note_text, ARRAY('medication_change', 'safety_concern', 'routine')) AS note_type,
       ai_mask(note_text, ARRAY('person', 'phone', 'email', 'address')) AS masked_text
FROM prod_clinical.silver.session_notes
WHERE note_date = current_date() - 1;

SELECT ai_query('<hosted-model-endpoint>',
                concat('Summarize the follow-up plan: ', masked_text)) AS plan
FROM prod_clinical.silver.notes_masked;

Model endpoint names vary by workspace and change as models are retired; check the serving page before hardcoding one.

• Submit the whole dataset in one AI function query; the engine parallelizes and retries. AI functions need DBR 15.4 LTS+ and do not run on classic SQL warehouses.
  • Billing: the compute running the query plus inference; task functions bill under AI_FUNCTIONS, ai_query under the serving endpoint, visible in system.billing.usage.
  • Hosted models retire frequently (several retirements in October 2026); parameterize model names and watch the retirement notices.
  • For PHI, confirm that the chosen model and region are covered by your compliance standard, and prefer Databricks-hosted models over external providers unless a BAA covers the provider.

Trap: Calling a scale-to-zero endpoint from a latency-sensitive app; the cold start breaks the SLA.
Trap: Looping ai_query row by row from Python; use a single set-based SQL query.
Trap: Sending unmasked PHI to an external model provider without contractual coverage.

• Which models are approved for PHI, and are they enforced through Unity Gateway policies?
  • Who owns spend limits for AI usage, including coding agents?
  • How are model retirements detected before they break a job?

cards.q: What is Unity Gateway?
cards.a: Databricks' control plane for governed access to models, MCP tools and skills, with routing, spend limits, guardrails and audit logs.

cards.q: Why is scale to zero not recommended for production model serving endpoints?
cards.a: Capacity is not guaranteed when scaled to zero, and scaling back up adds cold-start latency.

cards.q: Which SQL function sends a prompt to any supported model?
cards.a: ai_query.

cards.q: Can AI functions run on a classic SQL warehouse?
cards.a: No; AI functions are not available on classic SQL warehouses.

cards.q: Under which billing_origin_product do task-specific AI function costs appear?
cards.a: AI_FUNCTIONS in system.billing.usage.

concepts.n: Agent Bricks, MLflow 3 and AI Search
concepts.s: Agent Bricks is Databricks' developer platform for building and running custom agents, MLflow 3 provides tracing, evaluation, prompt registry and LoggedModel tracking, and AI Search (formerly Vector Search) provides governed vector, hybrid and full-text retrieval over Unity Catalog data.

x.b:
• Agent Bricks: code-first agents (any framework, with LangGraph and OpenAI Agents SDK templates) deployed to Agent Runtime, which runs the agent server on Databricks Apps and exposes /api/invocations. The Agent Bricks CLI (agentbricks init | dev | deploy) is Beta. Managed agent memory and sessions (Lakebase-backed) are Beta.
  • Knowledge Assistant and Supervisor Agent became legacy on October 12, 2026; Databricks directs low-code builders to Genie Agents.
  • MLflow 3: LoggedModel tracks a model across training, evaluation and deployment; GenAI tracing auto-instruments 20+ frameworks; mlflow.genai.evaluate with LLM judges; human feedback review; Prompt Registry in Unity Catalog; Unity Catalog is the default model registry.
  • AI Search (renamed from Vector Search June 1, 2026): Delta Sync indexes (managed or self-managed embeddings) or Direct Vector Access indexes; standard endpoints (up to about 320M vectors at 768 dimensions) or storage-optimized endpoints (over 1B vectors, faster indexing, roughly 250 ms extra latency); hybrid search with reciprocal rank fusion; full-text indexes in Beta.

• Evaluation is the gating step: build an evaluation dataset of real questions with expected answers, run judges in CI, and monitor production traces with the same scorers.
  • Delta Sync indexes need change data feed on the source; self-managed embedding indexes cannot be converted to Databricks-managed later.
  • Agents inherit governance from Unity Catalog and Unity Gateway; give each agent its own service principal with least privilege.
  • In MLflow 3, log models with name instead of artifact_path, and use mlflow.genai.evaluate for LLM apps since mlflow.evaluate is deprecated.

Trap: Building on Knowledge Assistant or Supervisor Agent now; both are legacy.
Trap: Shipping an agent without traces; you cannot debug or evaluate production behavior after the fact.
Trap: Choosing a storage-optimized endpoint for a latency-critical chat app, or a standard endpoint for a billion-vector corpus.

• What evaluation set and quality bar must an agent pass before production?
  • Which identity does the agent use for data access, and can it read PHI?
  • Which retrieval index type and endpoint type match the corpus size and latency target?

cards.q: What is Vector Search called as of June 2026?
cards.a: AI Search.

cards.q: Which MLflow 3 function evaluates GenAI apps with LLM judges?
cards.a: mlflow.genai.evaluate (mlflow.evaluate is deprecated).

cards.q: What are the two AI Search index types?
cards.a: Delta Sync indexes that sync from a source table, and Direct Vector Access indexes updated through the API.

cards.q: Where do Agent Bricks agents run?
cards.a: On Agent Runtime, which runs the agent server on Databricks Apps behind an invocations API.

cards.q: What is the status of Knowledge Assistant and Supervisor Agent?
cards.a: Legacy since October 2026; use Genie Agents for low-code or Agent Bricks for code-first agents.

concepts.n: Databricks Apps and Lakebase
concepts.s: Databricks Apps hosts Python and Node.js web apps on serverless compute next to governed data, and Lakebase is Databricks' managed, autoscaling Postgres for transactional app state, with synced tables that serve lakehouse data to apps at low latency.

x.b:
• Databricks Apps: Streamlit, Dash, Gradio, React, Express and similar frameworks; OAuth sign-in; each app has its own service principal and can also act on behalf of the user; resources include SQL warehouses, serving endpoints, secrets, Genie Agents and Lakebase databases. Billed per hour while running. Horizontal scaling and OpenTelemetry telemetry to Unity Catalog went GA in September 2026.
  • Lakebase: serverless Postgres with autoscaling, scale to zero, branching and instant restore. GA on AWS (January 2026), on Azure, and on GCP (October 30, 2026); available for HIPAA compliance-profile workspaces on AWS since March 2026.
  • Synced tables: read-only Postgres copies of Unity Catalog tables in snapshot, triggered or continuous mode; triggered and continuous need change data feed (write-time or automatic) on the source.
  • Lakebase Search (hybrid vector and full-text inside Postgres) is GA on AWS and Beta on GCP.

• Use Lakebase for row-level reads and writes from apps (forms, workflow state, feature lookups) and the lakehouse for analytics; synced tables bridge gold data to the app.
  • Synced tables: snapshot suits more than 10 percent change per cycle; continuous has a 15-second minimum interval and the highest cost; each source table supports up to 20 synced tables; changing a primary key requires recreating the synced table.
  • Branching lets you test schema migrations against a copy of production data without duplicating storage.
  • Prefer on-behalf-of-user authorization in apps that show PHI so Unity Catalog grants and masks apply per viewer.

Trap: Giving the app's service principal broad SELECT on PHI and filtering in app code; a bug exposes everything. Use user authorization or narrow grants.
Trap: Pointing an app's interactive reads at a SQL warehouse for single-row lookups; Lakebase or synced tables are built for that latency.
Trap: Running triggered synced tables every minute; intervals under five minutes are expensive.

• Does the app need transactional writes (Lakebase) or only analytical reads (SQL warehouse)?
  • Which identity does the app use to read data, and is it per user?
  • Which sync mode matches the freshness need and budget?

cards.q: What is Lakebase?
cards.a: Databricks' managed serverless Postgres with autoscaling, scale to zero and branching, integrated with Unity Catalog and Databricks Apps.

cards.q: What are the three Lakebase synced table modes?
cards.a: Snapshot, triggered and continuous.

cards.q: What do triggered and continuous synced tables require on the source table?
cards.a: A change data feed, either write-time CDF or automatic CDF.

cards.q: How are Databricks Apps billed?
cards.a: Per hour of compute while the app is running, based on provisioned capacity.

cards.q: How can a Databricks App enforce per-viewer data permissions?
cards.a: Use on-behalf-of-user authorization so queries run with the viewer's Unity Catalog permissions.
